costs.fee_source: Bybit Trading Fee Structure, VIP 0, perpetual and futures contracts: maker 0.0200%, taker 0.0550% (https://www.bybit.com/en/help-center/article/Trading-Fee-Structure, read 2026-11-19). Rates depend on account tier and change; set your own.
costs.maintenance_margin_source: Bybit risk limit, BTCUSDT tier 1 (positions up to 300,000 USDT): 0.33% (https://api.bybit.com/v5/market/risk-limit?category=linear&symbol=BTCUSDT, snapshot 2026-11-18). Other symbols and larger positions have higher rates.

timing.grid_start: open of the first bar of each sample
timing.grid_orders: fill when price trades strictly through the level, at the level

assumptions: intrabar path: each bar is walked twice, open-low-high-close and open-high-low-close; the path that leaves lower equity at the bar close is kept (pessimistic about the order of high and low, chosen bar by bar); the move from the previous close to the open is walked first
a cell that fills can trade again later in the same bar if the path crosses its other level
grid orders fill only when price trades strictly through their level, at the level price (never better), then slippage is applied against the trader
grid fills pay grid_fee_rate (maker); the initial position, range closes and the end-of-sample close are market orders and pay taker_fee_rate
the grid is placed at the open of each sample's first bar; each sample starts flat with the same capital, and anything open at its last bar is closed at that bar's close

isolated margin: the grid's whole equity backs its net position; liquidation when equity <= maintenance_margin_rate x |net quantity| x price, checked at every path end point; on liquidation the remaining equity is lost
funding: net quantity x bar close x Bybit's settled rate at every funding time (Bybit uses the mark price; the difference is ignored)

bounds are the lowest low and highest high of the in-sample period: known only in hindsight during the in-sample period, so the in-sample result is optimistic by construction; the out-of-sample period is the test

grid.bounds_source: in-sample lowest low and highest high

warnings: in_sample: the grid bounds come from the in-sample period itself, so this block is optimistic by construction; use out_of_sample as the test
disclaimer: Backtest on historical data. Not investment advice. Past results do not predict future results. Grid fills inside a bar are estimated from OHLC data under the stated path assumption.
